articles.title: Plans for Demolition of Flats in Lower Falinge Resurface
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has revealed new plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, sparking distress among remaining residents.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has announced plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, which contain 126 homes, as part of a redevelopment project. The new proposal aims to replace the existing structures with 270 new homes, including a mix of flats and houses, situated between St Mary’s Gate and Sheriff Street.

The maisonette blocks earmarked for demolition include Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, and Vaynor. Only the Zedburgh block, currently occupied by a couple, is still inhabited. Andy Roche, a resident since 1988, expressed his distress over the plans, stating that the eviction is making both him and his partner, who are autistic, feel unwell.

RBH previously faced a legal challenge that halted demolition plans last year, requiring them to present a clear vision for the area. Despite the new proposals, Roche feels that the concerns of residents have not been adequately addressed. He has been offered alternative housing options but claims none match his current living situation.

The estate has seen significant changes over the years, with previous phases of redevelopment resulting in 100 new homes. However, many blocks remain derelict, and Roche lamented the loss of community, noting that the area is now devoid of families and children.
